rows.what the ink shows: A closed initial oval is followed by a separate p stem descending below its small right shoulder, then a detached round dot. The o is overinked but retains its white upper counter.

Two baseline bodies survive the horizontal deletion: the left has two uprights joined by a deep u trough, and the right rises into a compact hooked v body. The immediately following uncancelled vu supplies the local hooked v and open u comparison; no superscript appears.

The word begins with a short i stroke and two low extended m runs; the middle retains a looped d and a detached i dot, followed by a tall t and compressed connected ending. It forms one run without the opening a/ss bodies or separate initial d required by aussi directement.

After the uncancelled L¹(E), the deleted group retains a left curved parenthesis, the upright and right-going bars of E, and a distinct closing hook at the right. Crossing strokes thicken the upper and middle bars without hiding the complete parenthetical extent.

The second deleted group has a separate curved left edge, an E with three rightward horizontal arms, and a closing parenthesis turning left at its foot. The cancellation follows the bars, but their joins and the two outside curves remain visible.

The deleted upper layer has visible opening and closing curved parentheses. Two heavy diagonal/horizontal strokes obscure the internal low letter bodies; the clearly readable lower inserted sur is a separate layer and does not establish all three deleted letters.

The initial barred body is crossed by several diagonal and vertical strokes, followed by a rightward shaft with a dark head. At the right a u-shaped body, small low loop, downward terminal hook and separate oblique dash survive; cancellation prevents secure separation of the proposed opening parenthesis, possible low index and punctuation, so the entire source fragment remains uncertain.

Between u=u₀ and the separate following comma is a tall, thick vertical cluster with an upper slant and a rightward spur. It is not a clean round dot; overinking prevents identifying the underlying punctuation or cancelled sign.

Supprimer retains the initial s/u run, paired p descenders, r rise, dotted i and low mer ending; comme has a co loop followed by successive low m shoulders and an e exit, while application has an initial a, paired p descenders, tall l, dotted i and extended tion ending. In the disputed upper middle, the small oval/flat exit and paired tall t strokes do not secure the complete ou mettre sequence; the first lower word has discontinuities through its s/i/m positions despite surviving p/l traces, so simple also remains uncertain.
The cancelled group has a curved left boundary merging with the E spine, three rightward E arms, and a distinct curved closing parenthesis; the middle is crossed by heavy horizontal strokes.

The single baseline letter has one rounded low trough, a short rise at the right, and a descending exit; there is no second separate trough for w. The two norm bars on each side remain separate from the letter.

A long dark cancellation covers the low bodies of both proposed words. An upright after the short initial group and a later c-like hook with several connected remnants survive, but do not distinguish the complete letter sequence est contenue.

The opening has m shoulders, a small detached a body, a low n connector, the separated dot and body of i, then a tall f with a deep lower return. After f the ink is compressed into a long connector and raised angular loop; the individual estement bodies are not separable, so a shortened ending cannot be excluded.

Despite the crossing stroke, two left bars, one curved baseline u, and two right bars remain visible. A distinct short lower-right hooked upright supplies the index 1; no second baseline factor or raised power appears in this cancelled group.

Inside the inserted radical are two left bars and one baseline u. At the right are two taller bar strokes followed by a separate third, lower hooked upright before the closing parenthesis, supporting the index 1; there is no additional baseline factor or raised power.

Below the radical insertion, a short initial curved stroke and low connected segment precede an upright and long dark cancellation ending in a loop. The crossing and nearby vertical stain prevent identifying every letter or securely reading sinon.

After the unmarked a, a shallow cup and several short shoulders survive along the cancelled suffix, with a thicker upright near its right end. The cancellation merges the middle letter bodies, and the lower baseline lies near the scan edge, so the complete urait sequence remains uncertain.

notes: Assigned M1145–M1153 only. Actual image size 1676×2159. Start timestamp was taken before the first own-ink view; text/instruction preparation preceded it.
M1150 keeps internal deleted letters uncertain independently of the readable lower insertion. M1151 and M1152 were sent to the coordinator for independent review.

M1153 has a complete rotated source-box view plus enlarged line views. A later targeted reinspection narrowed uncertainty to ou mettre and simple; supprimer, comme and application retain independent word-body support.
No OCR, recognition service or ImageGen used. All listed views were actually inspected; initial incorrect-direction margin rotation is retained in the view log.
The primary interval includes a gap after the initial finish and the separate revision interval; it is not continuous active-reading time. M1151 and M1152 remained unchanged after peer agreement.
